evidence: Liv. 34.50: prōsequentibus cūnctīs servātōrem līberātōremque acclāmantibus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: With the dative of the person. In Cicero it is mostly to shout someone down; the sense of cheering and applauding Lewis & Short finds from Livy on (Livy, Tacitus, Suetonius).

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 290.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
